extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent examiners, and inventors engaged in U.S. patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing examination, rejection, applicant responses, and amendments to U.S. patent applications (office-action practice, affidavits of priority, and limits on new matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner disclosure on lack of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ground of the rejection be the absence of novelty in the subject-matter of the application, the examiner must disclose to the applicant all his own information on the subject, citing the best references at his command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When references are prior patents, designate each by date and number, patentee's name, and class of the invention; when prior publication, give title, date, page/plate, and place of publication or where a copy may be procured; when the reference is a fact within the knowledge of the examiner or Office, provide as precise data as nature admits and support by affidavit. Explain pertinence of the reference if not obvious, and particularly specify the anticipated Claim relied on.

rubrics_metrics.name: References need not be identical or commercially valuable
rubrics_metrics.description: Devices cited as references need not have commercial value, nor be identical in form, material, or mode of use with that described in the application; substantial correspondence constituting them the same invention is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the parts of the reference relied on as accurately designated as possible when the reference shows other inventions than that claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned or rejected applications and prior disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned or rejected application is not a public document and cannot be referred to as disclosing prior knowledge of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful: the treatise records both statements and case citations; examine jurisdictional case law for contrary holdings before citing such applications as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must cite pertinent references and best first
rubrics_metrics.description: Pertinent references only should be mentioned, and the best references should be cited first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is under no obligation to suggest proper Claims to be inserted in the application; selection/order of cited references should reflect relevance and weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must give all reasons for rejection promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: That all the examiner's reasons for rejecting the application must be given at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References and objections are to be cited and urged by the examiner on or before final rejection; later raising of omitted references may be limited (see procedural rules regarding final rejection and appeals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of priority must be supported by affidavit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner denies the priority of the applicant he must support his denial by an affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits alleging facts in the examiner's personal knowledge should be used to support denials of priority; applicant may counter with affidavits or other proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responses to rejection (options)
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of notice of rejection the applicant may insist on allowance, amend the application, or withdraw it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If insisting, the applicant may controvert by argument on law or identity of the invention, or deny the facts in the cited references; opposing examiner's affidavits with applicant affidavits or depositions is permitted, and examiner may rebut with counter-proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of prior invention (affidavit contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: To overcome a prior patent or publication the applicant must show by competent legal proof that he had disclosed or completed the invention before the cited date and aver he does not know or believe the invention was in public use or on sale more than two years prior to his application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof should show reduction to practice or reasonable diligence in reduction before the filing date of the cited reference; affidavits must set out the facts on which the claim of prior invention is based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must produce drawings/models when relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant bases his claim on drawings or models, such drawings and models, or copies of them, must be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the applicant asserts the making of drawings/models to carry back a date, the originals or copies should be presented to substantiate the assertion (Ex parte Saunders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office may receive third-person affidavits but guard against fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office may receive affidavits of third persons in uncontested cases, but care must be taken to guard against fraud; the applicant must have an opportunity to examine them and offer counter-proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process: where affidavits allege public use or other facts adverse to applicant, notice and an opportunity to rebut are required; ex parte affidavits without notice/examination are improper in many contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits averring public use two years before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits averring that the invention was in public use two years before the application was filed authorize the Commissioner to call on the applicant to show cause why he should not prove the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such affidavits open inquiry and may require the applicant to rebut by affidavit or other proof; mere ex parte affidavits without examination may be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection on public use/sale requires notice and legal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: That the inquiry of the Commissioner into the knowledge of others as to an alleged public use is a judicial inquiry, and there must be due notice and legal evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination and opportunity to offer counter-evidence are important; a rejection on public use or sale on mere ex parte affidavits without notice/examination is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination and communication after applicant's proofs (second rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the applicant insists and completes proofs and counter-proofs upon disputed questions of fact, the examiner is required to re-examine the case and communicate the result; if he again rejects, his second rejection must specifically and exhaustively allege grounds of adverse decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second rejection must be as specific as the first; applicant is entitled to know all bases of rejection to prepare appeal or further amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments allowed before final disposition; limits on substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the application may be offered at any time after it is taken up for examination and before final disposition; amendments in form are optional or may be required, but amendments in substance can be made only within certain limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter can be introduced by amendment; amendments in form correct inaccuracies, undue prolixity, or secure correspondence between Claim and Description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and prohibition of new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter is that which is not found in the specification, drawings, or model as first filed, and which involves a departure from the original invention; such matter cannot be introduced by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment contains features not found in original filing (and not merely different modes of describing the same invention), it introduces new matter and must be filed as a separate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted supplemental amendments (no new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that merely supply suitable connections, add subordinate devices, remedy manifest defects, correct clerical errors, or declare further uses (i.e., completing the invention imperfectly shown) may be made without introducing new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These must agree with the construction and operation already presented and not change essential character; if drawings/models accompanied original, amendments must conform to at least one of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not substantially represented require new oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments not introducing new matter, but containing features not substantially represented in the original application, must be accompanied by a new oath averring that the subject of the amendment was part of the original invention and invented before the original filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such a new oath is filed, the date of the application is changed to that of the new oath for the amended matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment that changes character of invention forbidden
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments changing the essential character of the invention, altering construction or mode of operation, or describing a different embodiment are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may not, under the guise of amendment, introduce a wholly different invention or change operation/constructive meaning materially (Ex parte Snyder, Ex parte Wharton, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment cannot enlarge scope to prejudice others or appropriate intermediate inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment can be permitted to enlarge a specification to the prejudice of intermediate inventors; long delay in filing such amendments raises presumption of late discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts and the Office regard with jealousy attempts to enlarge an application after filing so as to appropriate what has gone into public use or been invented by others in the interim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment cannot insert matter in public use more than two years
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment cannot introduce into the application matter which has been in public use more than two years prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matter publicly used/known beyond statutory bars cannot be added; see cases cited (Kittle v. Hall etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amended in substance are treated as new (date and filing consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims amended in matters of substance are to be treated as new claims; when an amendment requiring a new oath is filed, the date of the application is changed to that of the new oath and is thereafter regarded as the true date of the amended application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can affect priority, intervening rights, and whether the amendment can antedate cited references; careful drafting and timely oath are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on timing of substantive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in substance cannot be filed on or after an appeal to the examiners-in-chief, nor after a notice of allowance has been given; after a second rejection the applicant cannot amend as a matter of course and must satisfactorily explain delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments should be completed before Claims are passed on by the examiner; if examiner refuses to receive, petition to Commissioner is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form requirements for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Every amendment must be written in a fair and legible hand, on one side of the paper, and on a separate sheet; no erasures can be made in the original application—the words to be stricken must be indicated and substitutions distinctly stated with place of insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a mandatory clause is amended it must be wholly rewritten so no erasure/interlineation appear; if amendments are numerous examiner may require entire specification be rewritten; specification cannot be taken from Office for alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and models constraints on amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When drawings and a model accompanied the original specification, amendments must conform to at least one of them; drawings must not be changed or erased in the Patent Office; an amendment introducing what was before shown only in the model requires a new oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no drawings/models, amendments must be shown by proper proof to have been embraced in the original invention; drawing/model withdrawal restrictions apply (cannot withdraw both at same time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate applications cannot qualify or support each other
rubrics_metrics.description: Two distinct applications cannot qualify or support each other; each application is regarded as that of an independent inventor and is in no manner affected by any other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A later application by the same inventor describing the same invention but claiming it more precisely is not an amendment of the earlier application; the earlier stands unaffected and may be amended independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must point out patentable novelty when offering amendment to overcome rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In offering an amendment to remove grounds of rejection the applicant must point out all the patentable novelty he thinks the case presents in view of the state of the art, and must show how his amendment avoids such references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner produces new references the applicant must address them; arguments should map claim elements to avoid cited art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition remedy when examiner refuses to receive amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner refuses to receive an amendment the applicant may petition the Commissioner, and unless the amendment is clearly improper the Commissioner may order the examiner to receive it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this procedural avenue when you believe an amendment is wrongly denied, but be aware the Commissioner will not favor clearly improper matters (e.g., new matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims filed after appeal to examiners-in-chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims filed after an appeal to the examiners-in-chief cannot be considered unless sanctioned by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims added post-appeal require Commissioner approval; do not expect unilateral acceptance by examiner after appellate referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after allowance/issue and final fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An application passed to issue in the form selected by applicant will not be withdrawn for amendment unless great damage would result; amendments in form may be made after the patent is ordered to issue and after payment of the final fee on recommendation of the examiner approved by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive broadening after allowance is disfavored; petitions to modify after allowance are limited and exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney cannot substitute a sworn specification
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney has no right to substitute a clean draft of a specification for the one signed and sworn to by the applicant; if he does so it must be erased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's signature and oath are crucial; attorneys should not attempt to replace the sworn specification without proper procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may act on Commissioner's personal knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office (or Commissioner) may act on his personal knowledge of public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, inquiry into knowledge of others is judicial and requires due notice and legal evidence; discretionary personal-knowledge decisions exist but are constrained by fairness requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits claiming priority against an existing patent are secret
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits claiming priority against an existing patent are secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural confidentiality applies to priority-contesting affidavits; their handling follows special rules.
